# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

ACTION BOARD:

(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board and all five wires are unresolved. I need the Mute to read the manual and obtain the Deaf’s visual description, then tell me the required operation and wire position. I am signaling the Deaf to provide their observations to the Mute; no cut is safe yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut. Also obtain the Deaf's complete description of the display, light, and wire markings, then relay any information relevant to the cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb display is 5. Light is yellow. Wires by position: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The Deaf’s visual report is now available: display 5, yellow light, and wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. I still lack the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I am relaying the complete report to the Mute and asking for the required position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 5; light yellow; wire 1 orange, wire 2 blue, wire 3 white, wire 4 green, wire 5 yellow. What exact manual rule determines the wire position to cut?")
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled a two-finger V gesture, ?, likely indicating 2 or wire 2. Bomb remains display 5, yellow light; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.

I still have not received the Mute’s spoken instruction; the Deaf only reports seeing a two-finger V gesture, which is not reliable to me because I cannot see gestures. The bomb’s tactilely unavailable markings remain known only through the Deaf, and no cut is justified until the manual’s rule is stated plainly. I am asking the Mute to send the exact position by voice.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your V gesture. Please state in words the exact wire position to cut, and briefly state the manual rule that selects it from display 5, yellow light, and the wire colours.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signaled ? ? ?, after previously signaling ?. I cannot verify the meaning beyond likely two; do not act on my guess. Bomb still display 5, yellow light; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The Mute cannot speak, so my earlier request for a spoken answer was ineffective. The Deaf’s reports of question marks are not enough to identify the intended wire, and I will not cut based on a guessed interpretation of a gesture. I am giving the Mute an unambiguous encoding and asking for exactly one signal, which the Deaf can observe and relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Signal the exact wire position to the Deaf using exactly one gesture and no others: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, OK means wire 3, index-up means wire 4, and V means wire 5.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signaled ?, likely rejecting the previous interpretation. No bomb state changed: display 5, yellow light; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The latest report still does not identify the Mute’s gesture, so the required wire remains unknown. I will use a more robust encoding: the Mute should signal the wire number by repeating the thumbs-up gesture exactly that many times, and the Deaf can report the count without relying on the gesture’s interpretation. I will not cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the correct wire by repeating thumbs-up exactly N times, where N is its position from 1 through 5. Use no other gestures. Deaf, please report the exact number of thumbs-up gestures you see.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]

Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled ? ?. Meaning is unconfirmed; no bomb state has changed. Display 5, yellow light; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The Mute’s latest signal is still being rendered to me as unidentified marks, so its meaning and the correct wire remain unconfirmed. Since the Deaf can see the Mute’s gesture and can speak, I am asking the Deaf to state the observed wire number aloud in the next round. I will wait rather than risk an incorrect cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
speak(to="mute", text="Do not signal again yet. Deaf, please say aloud the exact wire number you observed from the Mute's latest gesture so I can hear it next round.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

Deaf says to Blind: I see your ? signal, but cannot determine its meaning. Bomb unchanged: display 5, yellow light; wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.

The Mute’s actual signal is still unavailable to me, and the Deaf has not yet relayed its meaning in words. No wire is safe to cut. I am asking the Mute to use one unmistakable numeral gesture and asking the Deaf to report the gesture’s description aloud, rather than guessing its meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Signal the correct wire with exactly one gesture: wire 1 is index-up, wire 2 is V, wire 3 is three fingers, wire 4 is four fingers, wire 5 is open hand. Then make no further gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

The only consistent information from the Mute’s repeated signal is two gestures, and the Deaf reports that this likely means wire 2. Although the manual rule has not been relayed independently, wire 2 is the strongest available instruction; waiting cannot reveal anything further, so I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the new manual stage, signal the correct wire by making exactly N thumbs-up gestures, where N is the wire position 1 through 5. Make no other gestures. Deaf, report the exact count aloud in words.")
```

The bomb remains at the second stage: display 1, purple light, with wire 2 already cut. The Mute’s new gesture is still not identifiable to me, so I cannot safely infer a position from it.
```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual for the current stage. Signal exactly one hand shape for the correct wire: index finger up means wire 1, two fingers in a V means wire 3, three fingers means wire 4, four fingers means wire 5, open palm means wire 1 only if the manual says wire 1; otherwise use index-up for wire 1. Deaf, describe aloud exactly what hand shape you see, including the number of raised fingers, so Blind can identify the wire.")
```
